title: Kibble--Zurek Scaling in the Dicke Model at Mesoscopic Scales
abstract: The Dicke model is a paradigmatic setting for collective light-matter physics and the superradiant phase transition. Yet extracting the critical exponents is challenging at experimentally accessible mesoscopic sizes, due to the slow divergence of the correlation time under all-to-all coupling and a photon-loss-driven crossover to a distinct dissipative universality class. Here, we perform a large-$N$ analysis that identifies distinct coherent and dissipative fixed points for the closed and open Dicke models. We then develop a unified mesoscopic scaling framework that incorporates the leading irrelevant correction and, going beyond static and spectral probes, brings ramping dynamics under the same scaling description. It recovers the corresponding exponents, verifies Kibble-Zurek scaling, and clarifies how finite size, dissipation, and speed compete in the ramping dynamics. Our work thus establishes a unified framework for resolving static and dynamical critical scaling in closed and open quantum systems, with broader applicability to mesoscopic systems with long-range interactions.
summary: This paper develops a unified scaling framework to accurately determine critical exponents for the Dicke model at mesoscopic sizes. By incorporating leading irrelevant corrections, the authors successfully describe the critical dynamics across both coherent and dissipative regimes. This methodology offers a general approach for resolving static and dynamical critical scaling in various open quantum systems.
main_problem: The core challenge is extracting universal critical exponents for the Dicke model at mesoscopic scales, complicated by slow correlation time divergence and crossover into a dissipative universality class.
main_result: The authors establish a unified mesoscopic scaling framework that successfully recovers the Kibble-Zurek exponents for both closed and open quantum systems, clarifying the competition between finite size, dissipation, and ramping speed.
method: The work employs large-N analysis within a unified Keldysh field theory, developing a multi-stage finite-size scaling protocol that incorporates leading irrelevant corrections.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Dicke model, a paradigmatic system for collective light-matter physics exhibiting a superradiant phase transition. It is analyzed in both closed (Hamiltonian) and open (Lindblad equation) system settings.
key_observables:
Critical exponents ($
u, z, \mu$), Binder ratio ($U(N)$), and the soft-mode spectral gap ($\Delta(N)$).
important_parameters: Dissipation rate ($\kappa$), particle number ($N$), and ramping speed ($s$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the validity of large-N expansions and the ability to map the dynamics onto a unified scaling variable that accounts for irrelevant corrections.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram distinguishing closed/open classes, the scaling protocol involving irrelevant exponents, and the confirmation of scaling laws for both coherent and dissipative regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the challenge of mesoscopic critical dynamics, then developing the unified scaling framework using large-N methods, and finally applying this framework to extract and verify the exponents for both the closed and open Dicke models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalizable theoretical tool for analyzing critical dynamics in complex, open quantum systems where experimental access to the thermodynamic limit is impossible.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Phase diagram of the Dicke model in the plane of light-matter coupling g and dissipation κ. Two distinct universality classes are identified at large N: closed (green) and open (red). The ramp protocol is defined by the ramping speed s. (b) Crossover regions set by size N, dissipation κ, and speed s in the ramping dynamics. (c) Scaling protocol at mesoscopic scales that encodes the irrelevant exponent ω. The exponents ν, z, and µ are then extracted independently, and the KZ relation 1/µ = 1/ν + z is tested.

FIG. 3. Open Dicke model. (a) Joint critical Binder-ratio fit for different κ ∈[0.1, 3], used to fix ω. Red dashed curves show extrapolated U(N) vs κ at fixed N = 102, 103, 104, and N →∞, ordered from sparse to dense. (b)–(d) Extraction of z, ν, and µ from the Liouvillian gap, Binder-ratio derivative, and linear small-speed response, respectively. Insets in (b)– (d) show the corresponding κ dependence.

FIG. 2. Closed Dicke model. (a) Critical Binder ratio used to fix the leading irrelevant exponent ω. The red dashed line marks extrapolated U(N →∞). (b)–(d) Extraction of z, ν, and µ from the critical gap, Binder-ratio derivative, and small-speed response, respectively. Gray dashed curves in- clude corrections to scaling up to j = 2; green dashed lines show the leading power laws with the fitted exponents. For all figures, we set ω0 = ωz = 1.

FIG. 4. (a) Ramped Binder ratio in the closed Dicke model for different system sizes; red dashed lines indicate the N →∞ extrapolation. (b) Comparison of the ramped Binder ratio between the closed and open Dicke models for different κ.

FIG. 5. Soft-mode spectral gap of the open Dicke model at the critical point, obtained within the Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov approximation for κ = 1. The calculation is performed over the range N = 105–107, where the asymptotic N −1/2 decay becomes clearly visible.

Partially Pumped Collective Emitters.note: The new paper analyzes the Dicke model, which describes superradiant phase transitions, and its framework for open systems (Lindblad equation) is directly applicable to understanding collective decay dynamics in partially pumped emitter arrays.
